Improved summary uses action verb 'Look up' and clarifies that multiple rates may apply. data.current_summary: Minimum wage at a place and date
data.current_description: Every minimum wage that applies at a location on a date: federal, state (or a state region such as New York City or the Portland metro area), county and city, with the one that governs, the tipped minimum cash wage, other rates for defined groups (youth, small employers, hotels, fast food, health care), the next scheduled change and changes whose amount isn't announced yet. Every rate carries its official source and the date we last checked it. Give an address or coordinates for an exact answer: they resolve to a Census county and incorporated place, so unincorporated areas and towns that opted out of a county ordinance come out right. A city and county name works too, and the response lists under may_apply any rate that depends on details a name can't settle. When a state's own rate depends on the county (Oregon), minimum_wage is null until you pass one. other_rates lists the group rates under each law that covers the location. Each employee is owed the highest rate that covers them, so a lower state or federal group rate doesn't override a city or county rate unless the local law exempts that group. Canada: pass the province code as state. Plans: federal and state rates are on every plan; city and county rates by name need Developer, and address or coordinate lookups need Business. On the Free plan, a lookup where a local rate applies returns minimum_wage: null and a local_rates note instead of a figure a local rate overrides.
data.summary_suggestion: Look up applicable minimum wage rates
